enhanced.fullText:
The Byrd Amendment, codified at 31 U.S.C. § 1352 and implemented through 28 CFR Part 69, establishes comprehensive restrictions on the use of federal funds for lobbying activities by recipients of federal contracts, grants, loans, or cooperative agreements exceeding $100,000. This regulation is particularly significant for higher education institutions that receive substantial federal funding through research grants, student aid programs, and other federal assistance.

Under 31 U.S.C. § 1352(a), recipients are prohibited from using federal funds to pay any person for influencing or attempting to influence federal officers or employees in connection with the awarding, extension, continuation, renewal, amendment, or modification of federal contracts, grants, loans, or cooperative agreements. This prohibition extends to subrecipients and contractors at all tiers. Universities must ensure that federal grant funds are not used to support institutional lobbying efforts directed at Congress or federal agencies regarding pending legislation or regulatory matters.

The disclosure requirements under 31 U.S.C. § 1352(b) mandate that institutions submit Standard Form LLL (Disclosure of Lobbying Activities) when they engage in lobbying activities using non-federal funds in connection with federal awards. Universities must file this form quarterly for each federal action exceeding $100,000 where lobbying has occurred. The disclosure must identify the federal program, lobbying registrant, individuals performing services, recipients of payments, and specific issues lobbied.

28 CFR § 69.110 requires institutions to obtain certifications from subrecipients and contractors that they will comply with lobbying restrictions and disclosure requirements. Universities must include anti-lobbying clauses in all covered agreements and maintain documentation of compliance efforts. The regulation applies to all federal assistance, including Department of Education grants, National Science Foundation awards, and Department of Health and Human Services funding.

Violations can result in civil penalties up to $100,000 per violation under 31 U.S.C. § 1352(c), suspension or debarment from federal programs under 2 CFR Part 180, and potential criminal prosecution for knowing and willful violations. The 2007 amendments clarified that the prohibition applies to grassroots lobbying communications and expanded disclosure requirements for coalition memberships involving lobbying activities.
enhanced.summary: The Byrd Amendment (31 U.S.C. § 1352) prohibits universities from using federal funds for lobbying and requires disclosure when non-federal funds are used for lobbying related to federal awards exceeding $100,000.
enhanced.requirements:
## Prohibition Requirements
- Universities must not use federal funds to influence federal officers regarding contracts, grants, or cooperative agreements per 31 U.S.C. § 1352(a)
- Prohibition extends to all subrecipients and contractors at every tier
- Compliance officers must segregate federal and non-federal funding for lobbying activities

## Disclosure Obligations
- File Standard Form LLL quarterly for federal actions exceeding $100,000 where lobbying occurs using non-federal funds
- Submit disclosures within 30 days of lobbying activity commencement under 28 CFR § 69.100
- Update filings quarterly until federal action is completed

## Subrecipient Management
- Obtain written certifications from all subrecipients and contractors per 28 CFR § 69.110
- Include required anti-lobbying clauses in covered agreements
- Monitor subrecipient compliance and maintain documentation
enhanced.reportingRequirements: Standard Form LLL must be filed quarterly within 30 days of lobbying activity commencement for federal awards exceeding $100,000. Updates required every quarter until federal action completion. Submit to cognizant federal agency.
